'''Pradyut Ghosh''' (born 17 February 1970) is an Indian [[Inorganic chemistry|inorganic chemist]] and a professor at the [[Indian Association for the Cultivation of Science]].<ref name="Brief Profile of the Awardee">{{Cite web |url=http://ssbprize.gov.in/Content/Detail.aspx?AID=508 |title=Brief Profile of the Awardee |date=2016 |publisher=Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Prize |access-date=12 November 2016}}</ref> He is known for his studies on chemical sensing of [[anions]], interlocked molecules and [[self-assembly]].<ref name="Speaker profile">{{Cite web |url=http://www.ias.ac.in/82ndAM2016/Speakers/Pradyut_Ghosh |title=Speaker profile |date=2016 |publisher=Indian Academy of Sciences}}</ref> He is a recipient of the Swarnajayanthi Fellowship of the [[Department of Science and Technology (India)|Department of Science and Technology]] and the Bronze Medal of the [[Chemical Research Society of India]].<ref name="The New Global Research Hotspot: Molecular Magic">{{Cite web |url=https://www.indiatoday.in/magazine/science-and-technology/story/20110919-indian-scientists-at-forefront-of-research-pradyut-ghosh-747588-2011-09-10 |title=The New Global Research Hotspot: Molecular Magic |date=10 September 2011 |publisher=India Today}}</ref> The [[Council of Scientific and Industrial Research]], the apex agency of the Government of India for scientific research, awarded him the [[Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Prize for Science and Technology]], one of the highest Indian science awards, in 2015, for his contributions to chemical sciences.<ref name="View Bhatnagar Awardees">{{cite web | url=http://ssbprize.gov.in/Content/AwardeeList.aspx | title=View Bhatnagar Awardees | publisher=Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Prize | date=2016 | access-date=12 November 2016}}</ref>

== Biography ==
[[File:Kolkata univ jeroje.jpg|thumb|235px|left|University of Calcutta]]
Born on 17 February 1970 in a farmers' family in the village of [[Birsingha]] in [[Medinipur District]] of the Indian state of [[West Bengal]],<ref name="The New Global Research Hotspot: Molecular Magic" /> Pradyut Ghosh graduated in chemistry in 1990. He followed it up with a master's degree in 1992 from the [[Rajabazar Science College]], [[Calcutta University]].<ref name="Faculty profile">{{Cite web |url=http://mailweb.iacs.res.in/inorg/icpg/ |title=Faculty profile |date=2016 |publisher=Indian Association for the Cultivation of Science |access-date=8 December 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161220092237/http://mailweb.iacs.res.in/inorg/icpg/ |archive-date=20 December 2016 |url-status=dead }}</ref> Enrolling for his doctoral studies under the guidance of Parimal K. Bharadwaj at the [[Indian Institute of Technology, Kanpur]],<ref name="Display Alumni Newsmakers">{{Cite web |url=http://www.iitkalumni.org/displayalumninewsmakers.aspx |title=Display Alumni Newsmakers |date=2016 |publisher=IITK Alumni Association}}</ref> he secured a PhD in 1998 and moved to the US to pursue his post-doctoral studies under [[Richard M. Crooks]]. Returning to India in 2000, he joined the [[Central Salt and Marine Chemicals Research Institute]] (CSMCRI) as a scientist. In 2001, he received an [[Alexander von Humboldt Foundation|Alexander von Humboldt fellowship]] which enabled him to continue his professional studies with Fritz Vögtle and Christoph Schalley<ref name="Former Schalley Lab Members">{{Cite web |url=http://www.bcp.fu-berlin.de/en/chemie/chemie/forschung/OrgChem/schalley/Group_Members/index.html |title=Former Schalley Lab Members |date=2016 |website=Schalley Lab Homepage}}</ref> at the Kekulé Institute of Organic Chemistry and Biochemistry of the [[University of Bonn]]. He resumed his duties at CSMCRI in 2002 as a C-Grade Scientist, a post he held till 2007 during which time he had a second spell at Bonn University from April to October 2003. In 2007, he joined the [[Indian Association for the Cultivation of Science]] as an assistant professor where he served as the head of the department of inorganic chemistry from 2012 to 2015 and is a professor there.<ref name="Faculty profile" />

== Legacy ==
Ghosh is reported to have done extensive researches on [[Anion]] recognition, molecular capsules, chemical sensing of [[Ions]], inorganic salt extraction, [[Supramolecular assembly|supramolecular]] aggregations and interlocking molecules.<ref name="Faculty profile" /> He has developed several [[ligands]] with varying anion recognition elements as well as methodologies for selective sensing of phosphates, separation of hydrated metal sulphates/[[potassium bromide]] and [[bromide]] removal using [[halogen bonding]].<ref name="Speaker profile" /> The development of [[Gypsum]] chalk replacing the [[calcium carbonate]]-made chalk which was in use traditionally was one of his notable contributions.<ref name="The New Global Research Hotspot: Molecular Magic" /> His research has been documented by way of a number of peer-reviewed articles;<ref name="Publications">{{Cite web |url=http://mailweb.iacs.res.in/inorg/icpg/p_ghosh_complete_publication.html |title=Publications |date=2016 |publisher=Indian Association for the Cultivation of Science}}</ref> [[ResearchGate]], an online repository of scientific articles, has listed 112 of them.<ref name="On ResearchGate">{{Cite web |url=https://www.researchgate.net/profile/Pradyut_Ghosh |title=On ResearchGate |date=2016 }}</ref> He holds a patent for the process developed by him viz. ''Process for the recovery of palladium from spent silica''.<ref name="Process for the recovery of palladium from spent silica">{{Cite web |url=http://patents.justia.com/patent/7108839 |title=Process for the recovery of palladium from spent silica |author1=Arvindkumar Balvantrai Boricha |author2=Hari Chand Bajaj |author3=Raksh Vir Jasra |author4=Pradyut Ghosh |author5=Pushipito Kumar Ghosh |date=19 September 2006 |publisher=US Patent|work=Patent No. 7108839}}</ref> He was on the national organizing committee of the inaugural ''Frontiers of Organometallic Chemistry'', a biennial symposium on [[Organometallics]] held at [[Thiruvananthapuram]] in December 2016.<ref name="National Organising Committee">{{Cite web |url=http://iiti.ac.in/people/~fomc/ |title=National Organising Committee |date=2016 |publisher=Frontiers of Organometallic Chemistry}}</ref> He has delivered several invitational and plenary addresses.<ref name="Speaker profile" /> He has also mentored several scholars in their doctoral and post-doctoral studies.<ref name="Dr. Purnandhu Bose">{{Cite web |url=http://www.nims.go.jp/reticular/Purnandhu.html |title=Dr. Purnandhu Bose |date=2016 |publisher=NIMS}}</ref> He has been involved in a number of projects for agencies such as the Council of Scientific and Industrial Research, [[The World Academy of Sciences]], the Department of Science and Technology of India and the [[Science and Engineering Research Board]].<ref name="Sponsored Projects">{{Cite web |url=http://mailweb.iacs.res.in/inorg/icpg/p_ghosh_sponsored_projects.html |title=Sponsored Projects |date=2016 |publisher= Indian Association for the Cultivation of Science}}</ref>

== Awards and honors ==
Ghosh received the Young Scientist Award of the [[Indian Science Congress Association]] in 1998,<ref name="ISCA Young Scientist Award">{{Cite web |url=http://www.sciencecongress.nic.in/html/young_scientists_awards.php |title=ISCA Young Scientist Award |date=2016 |publisher=Indian Science Congress Association}}</ref> and the Young Scientist Award of the Council of Scientific and Industrial Research in 2004.<ref name="CSIR Young Scientist Award">{{Cite web |url=http://csirhrdg.res.in/ysa.htm |title=CSIR Young Scientist Award |date=2016 |publisher=Council of Scientific and Industrial Research}}</ref> The [[Brij Mohan Birla|B. M. Birla]] Science Prize in Chemical Sciences was awarded to him in 2009,<ref name="B. M. Birla Science Prize">{{Cite web |url=http://www.birlasciencecentre.org/awards/birlaSciencePrizes/ |title=B. M. Birla Science Prize |date=2016 |publisher=B. M. Birla Science Centre |access-date=8 December 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180128175901/http://www.birlasciencecentre.org/awards/birlaSciencePrizes/ |archive-date=28 January 2018 |url-status=dead }}</ref> the same year as he received the Swarnajayanthi Fellowship of the [[Department of Science and Technology (India)|Department of Science and Technology]].<ref name="The New Global Research Hotspot: Molecular Magic" /> This was followed by the Bronze Medal of the [[Chemical Research Society of India]] in 2012.<ref name="CRSI Bronze Medal">{{Cite web |url=http://crsi.org.in/index.php/crsi-awards/year-2012 |title=CRSI Bronze Medal |date=2016 |publisher=Chemical Research Society of India}}</ref> The Council of Scientific and Industrial Research honored him again with the [[Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Prize]], one of the highest Indian science awards, in 2015.<ref name="Chemical Sciences">{{cite web | url=http://www.csir.res.in/External/Heads/career/award/BPRIZE/CHEMICAL_SCIENCES.htm | title=Chemical Sciences | publisher=Council of Scientific and Industrial Research | date=2016 | url-status=dead | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120912012851/http://www.csir.res.in/external/heads/career/award/BPRIZE/CHEMICAL_SCIENCES.htm | archive-date=2012-09-12 }}</ref>
